convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load the 'BinaryWave' custom indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) for smoothing algorithms and trade execution logic. The custom indicator is not a built-in MT5 indicator, requiring recreation in Python.

derived_values.name: min_rates_1: max baseline period for data start
min_rates_2: baseline plus smoothing start bars
min_rates_total: minimum bars required for calculation

other_exits: In twist mode, position closes when BinaryWave direction changes (Value[1]>Value[2] for long close, Value[1]<Value[2] for short close)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Negative MM value is treated as fixed lot size (0.1 lots); positive MM value is treated as deposit fraction for position sizing, handled by TradeAlgorithms.mqh

custom_logic_notes: EA has two operating modes selectable via Mode input: 'breakdown' (zero-line crossover) and 'twist' (direction change). In breakdown mode, entry is triggered when BinaryWave crosses zero (Value[0]<=0 and Value[1]>0 for buy). In twist mode, entry is triggered when BinaryWave direction changes (Value[0]>Value[1] and Value[1]<Value[2] for buy). The BinaryWave indicator itself is a weighted composite of 7 standard indicators (MA, MACD, OsMA, CCI, Momentum, RSI, ADX), each binarized and summed with configurable weights, then smoothed with JJMA. SignalBar parameter (default 1) shifts which bar is used for signal detection. Separate boolean gates control buy/sell open and close permissions independently.
python_conversion_notes: Must recreate the BinaryWave composite indicator: binarize each of the 7 sub-indicators (+1 if bullish, -1 if bearish), multiply by their respective weights, sum them, then smooth with JJMA algorithm (which itself must be reimplemented from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh). The TradeAlgorithms.mqh must also be reverse-engineered for BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose functions including the MM negative-lot vs deposit-fraction logic, signal time tracking, and deviation handling. Two entry mode branches (breakdown vs twist) must both be implemented. SL/TP are in points (1000/2000) which are large values suggesting 5-digit broker compatibility is already baked in.
